content:
**Built the supersedes writer (#805): memory:save --supersedes <id>, local-first store check, fail-closed on a degraded upstream, refusal before any write; the record-first correction sequence drafted**

**What**: Added brain/scripts/memory/lib/supersedes.mjs (classifySupersedes: malformed | not-in-store | could-not-verify | ok; local ids first, origin/main only on a miss; the upstream reader's reason quoted verbatim with both remedies named), threaded --supersedes through plainfiles.save with seams and a refusal BEFORE buildRecord (nothing hashed, scanned or appended), enforced exactly one id in the CLI (a repeated flag, a value-less flag and the --supersedes=<id> form are all refused, never silently dropped), named the flag in engram.save's unsupportedOp, eight i18n keys, an integration test on a temp repo with a local bare origin (chains, upstream-only id, unknown id, degraded upstream, memory:audit coverage.supersedes 0 to 1, the field surviving reindex), and brain-drafts/memory-backend-contract.draft.md adding the record-first four-step correction sequence after the Deletion ruling (planAmendment ok, idempotent).

**Why**: epic #864 task 2.1; ADR-0034 L2 makes this the gate for ENABLING the lane's auto-merge: a wrong record is undone by a record, never by a rewrite. The ticket's own sequence contradicted the deletion ruling; the draft reconciles it.

**Where**: brain/scripts/memory/lib/supersedes.mjs, supersedes.test.mjs, supersedes.integration.test.mjs; backends/plainfiles.mjs; cli.mjs; backends/engram.mjs (message only); brain/scripts/i18n/{en,es}.mjs; openspec/changes/issue-805-supersedes-writer/**.

**Learned**: the memory CLI's flag parser is last-wins and cannot tell a value-less flag from an absent one, so a declared field can vanish silently; every new flag needs its own arity guards. upstreamRecordEntries returns byId (a Map), not entries. A fresh cold review killed nine mutants and found the = form; fixed before the push. The reader that resolves a chain to its tip is deferred to #874/#880 on purpose.
